NAGA FLOOD WATCH

See the Flood. Track the Changes. Protect the Community.

Naga Flood Watch is a web-based and Android-accessible application designed to improve flood awareness and disaster preparedness in Naga City, Camarines Sur, Philippines. Developed in response to NASA's Dancing with the SARs challenge, our project highlights the potential of satellite technology and interactive mapping to help communities better understand flood risks.

The application combines flood-susceptibility maps, interactive timelines, and rainfall-based simulations to visualize how flooding may develop and spread over time. It also provides weather forecasts, barangay flood-risk information, emergency hotlines, mapped evacuation locations, and suggested travel guidance.

Our project addresses the challenge by demonstrating how flood information could be presented through an accessible platform, with future plans to incorporate NASA's NISAR radar observations for satellite-based flood detection and monitoring.

Naga Flood Watch is important because communities need understandable and accessible information to prepare for disasters. Although the current flood simulations are illustrative rather than verified forecasts, our project lays the foundation for a more data-driven disaster preparedness tool that aims to strengthen community awareness, safety, and resilience.
details:
NAGA FLOOD WATCH

Naga Flood Watch is a web-based and Android-accessible flood awareness and disaster preparedness application developed for Naga City, Camarines Sur, Philippines. Inspired by NASA's Dancing with the SARs challenge, our project aims to demonstrate how satellite technology and interactive mapping can help communities better understand flooding and prepare for emergencies.

The application features an interactive satellite map that highlights flood-prone areas and visualizes possible flood movement. Its Timeline feature allows users to observe simulated flooding across different days and hours, while the Prediction feature illustrates how floodwater might spread under light, moderate, and heavy rainfall conditions. It also includes an Emergency section with barangay flood-risk information, emergency hotlines, and mapped evacuation locations. Additional features include daily weather forecasts and suggested travel guidance.

Our project aims to make flood-related information more accessible, understandable, and useful to residents, particularly those living in flood-prone communities. By bringing flood visualizations and emergency resources together, Naga Flood Watch promotes disaster awareness, preparedness, and community resilience.

We developed the application using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet.js, QGIS, and GeoJSON, along with Esri satellite basemaps and Open-Meteo weather data. GitHub Pages was used for deployment, while PWABuilder enabled Android application packaging.

What makes Naga Flood Watch unique is its interactive approach to flood awareness. Rather than relying only on static hazard maps, users can explore different rainfall scenarios, observe changes in simulated flood coverage, and locate marked evacuation sites within a single mobile-friendly platform.

During development, our team prioritized accessibility, ease of use, local flood vulnerability, and responsible communication of risk. We also considered data limitations and the importance of verified information for emergency decision-making.

Although the current flood simulations are illustrative rather than official forecasts, our long-term goal is to incorporate NASA NISAR radar observations, GPM IMERG rainfall estimates, and SRTM elevation data to support more reliable flood monitoring.

Ultimately, Naga Flood Watch seeks to empower communities through accessible technology, helping build a safer, more informed, and flood-resilient Naga City.
